extract:
Leiva is the stage name of José Miguel Conejo Torres, a singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist from Madrid, Spain. He first came to prominence in the late 1990s and 2000s as one half of Pereza, the Madrid rock duo he formed with Rubén Pozo. After Pereza went on hiatus around 2011, he launched a solo career in 2012 that has made him one of the most successful figures in contemporary Spanish rock and pop. He has stayed continuously active since, both as a performer and as a writer and producer for other artists.

His formative years were rooted in the Madrid rock tradition and in classic Anglo-American rock. The Rolling Stones and Bob Dylan sat alongside local reference points such as Tequila, Burning and Rosendo. With Pereza he refined a guitar-driven, Stones-indebted sound across albums such as Algo para cantar, Animales, Aproximaciones and Baires. That run turned the duo into an arena-level act in Spain and gave him the grounding in hooks and street-level lyricism that would carry into his solo work.

His solo debut, Diciembre (2012), was introduced by singles including Eme and Anticiclón. It presented a more introspective, cantautor-leaning songwriter while keeping the rock backbone of his earlier band. Singles like Afuera en la Ciudad and Terriblemente Cruel bridged into his second album, Pólvora (2014), which brought tracks such as Mirada Perdida and consolidated his status as a headliner. Monstruos (2016) continued that ascent with a darker, more textured palette. Nuclear (2019) became one of his most ambitious records, followed by singles such as Mi Pequeño Chernóbil and La Estación Eterna in 2020. Partido a Partido, released that same year, borrows the motto associated with Atlético de Madrid manager Diego Simeone, a nod to Leiva's well-known devotion to the club.

Collaboration has been central to his career. The 2015 track Sixteen brought him together with Fito Cabrales of Fito & Fitipaldis and Carlos Tarque of M Clan, three pillars of Spanish rock from the same generation. His most celebrated partnership was with Joaquín Sabina, for whose album Lo niego todo (2017) Leiva served as a key co-writer and producer, helping revitalize the veteran's sound. He has also moved in close orbit with figures such as Ariel Rot and Iván Ferreiro, reflecting his position at the center of the Spanish rock community.

Critical recognition peaked with La Llamada (2017), the title song for the film by Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi. It earned him the Goya Award for Best Original Song, an honor that extended his reach beyond the rock audience into broader Spanish popular culture. His albums have regularly topped the Spanish charts, and his tours fill arenas, including large venues in his native Madrid. His crossover appeal accounts for his presence in both indie and arena pop circles.

Leiva remains an active touring and recording artist and continues to release new solo material and produce for others. He has also reunited with Rubén Pozo for Pereza concerts, revisiting the band that launched him. His legacy rests on having carried the spirit of classic Madrid rock into the 21st century, through his own records and through his work behind the scenes for some of Spain's most revered songwriters.
title: Leiva
